text: I’ll review the stdio flush and seek paths, then make a conservative candidate with host tests for seek counts and failure semantics. I’ll keep the frozen E70 build untouched and record the source hash and diff with the evidence.

The safest fast path is limited to descriptor-backed streams with buffered read data and `SEEK_SET`. It can seek directly while holding the stream lock, then discard the read buffer on success. On failure it can preserve the buffer and logical position. Cookie streams will retain their existing callback sequence, and output streams will still flush before seeking.

The candidate is now in the maintained source tree. The host fixture will compile the actual NuttX read, write, flush, seek, tell and ungetc code against real temporary files. It will compare seek counts and cover failed seeks, partial writes, cookie callbacks and lock balance.

The host tests pass under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. For 1,000 buffered reads, both read-only and update streams drop from 1,999 seeks to 1,000; reads remain at 1,000. The tests also confirm output flushing, cookie callbacks, errno, EOF, pushback and lock handling. Hardware performance remains unmeasured.

Implemented the conservative candidate in [lib_fseeko.c](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/openvela-dev/nuttx/libs/libc/stdio/lib_fseeko.c:81): 30 inserted lines, limited to descriptor-backed buffered `SEEK_SET`.

Actual NuttX libc host tests passed all six configurations, totaling 102 scenario checks under ASan/UBSan. Buffered 1,000-read loops now perform **1,000 seeks instead of 1,999**, with 1,000 reads unchanged. Tests cover output flushing, partial/failed writes, failed seeks and recovery, EOF/ungetc, cookie callbacks and recursive locks. `nxstyle` and whitespace checks passed.

[Evidence and reproduction instructions](/home/regex/work/esp32s31-openvela/backups/xts-adaptation-and-test-evidence/korvo-fs-stdio-seek/README.md) include the exact patch, before/after source snapshots, hashes and test receipts. Applying the patch to the E70 original reproduces the candidate exactly. Frozen E70 remains unchanged.

Ready for an isolated E70-based A/B build. No firmware build or hardware operation performed; performance gains remain unmeasured. The intentional failure-path change retains buffered input and pushback after a failed absolute descriptor seek; cookie behavior stays on its existing path.
